newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: La Tondena reports one-time gains in 1996.
newsitem.headline: La Tondena reports one-time gains in 1996.

text.p: La Tondena Distillers Inc, a unit of San Miguel Corp, said on Thursday its net income in 1996 rose 40 percent to 914 million pesos from 652 million pesos in 1995, which included one-time gains of 186 million pesos from a property sale.
Stripped of non-recurring items, net income was 728 million pesos in 1996, up 19 percent from 611 million pesos in 1995, the company said in a statement.
Considered as the country's leader in the hard liquor industry, La Tondena generated net sales of 7.695 billion pesos, 31 percent higher than 5.888 billion pesos in 1995.

The company said its liquor sales volume slowed down with a growth of about 4.0 percent in 1996 due to price increases from higher raw material costs and deferments of orders by wholesalers adjusting to higher operating capital required by the shift to plastic crates from cartons.
But La Tondena said vigorous growth came from its mineral water business and acquisition of the juice business of SMC Juice Inc, another unit of San Miguel.
Further growth is expected in the mineral water business when its second bottling plant starts commercial operations in the first quarter of this year, it said.
"LTDI is confident that the company will manifest a more sizeable improvement in 1997," the statement said, adding that the company planned various expansion programmes before the end of the year.
It was also able to consolidate control of one of its alcohol suppliers last year which would give La Tondena a steady supply of alcohol in the years ahead.
